subject: RT spike: hosted API p95/p99 tail jump impacting Aurora Health
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@aurora-health.com>
To: support@redwood.com; rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: ops@aurora-health.com; tom.park@aurora-health.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 jump — production impact right now

Hi Rafael / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sharp increase in request latency starting ~07:45 UTC across our EU and US users. p95 for text-generation calls jumped from ~210ms to ~840ms and p99 is spiking above 2s which is impacting our real-time triage UI. Errors are also creeping up (~0.6% -> 2.3%). This started without any deployment on our side. Can you confirm whether something on your end changed?

We've attached a short capture and a few sample request IDs. We need this diagnosed quickly — this is affecting clinician workflows.

Att: aurora-p95-logs-20280301.zip

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Production Ops Lead, Aurora Health

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 jump — production impact right now

Team — quick summary of what infra found (initials):
- No model rollout or kernel swap in hosted model catalog at ~07:40 UTC.
- Metrics: regional edge egress from us-central to eu-west shows elevated RTTs beginning 07:42 UTC.
- Observed a surge of routed sessions from eu-west customers being egressed via our us-central peering for ~30m windows; that explains simultaneous US+EU symptom.
- Correlation: p95 jump aligns with increased cross-region hop count and packet RTTs from our edge.

I believe this is a routing policy mismatch: an automated failover policy pushed traffic to the wrong peering for a subset of sessions (policy version 2.7.9 rollback scheduled). I'm escalating to network ops to flip targeted route config and validate path.

Immediate next steps:
1) Network ops to rollback offending egress policy for affected edge cluster (in progress).
2) Throttle burst routing to force session re-bind to local edge on Aurora tenant.
3) Post-mitigate: run prefix-level trace and validate p95/p99 in 10m windows.

I'll stand by for logs and will update when routes are confirmed corrected.

Karthik
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com; jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 12:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 jump — production impact right now

Alyssa, Rafael —
Following Karthik's note: Network ops performed a targeted rollback of egress policy 2.7.9 at 11:02 UTC for the affected edge cluster. We then forced session rebinds for Aurora's tenant on their region bindings. Post-rollback telemetry (11:10-11:30 UTC) shows p95 dropping back to ~240ms and p99 below 800ms. Error rate also returned to baseline.

We're continuing with a 60-minute observation window and will keep the Aurora support line in the loop. I'm also filing a postmortem and will attach the timeline and RCA. For affected SLAs, we will open a credit request and coordinate with finance.

Short-term remediation performed:
- rollback egress policy for cluster-aurora-edge-02
- rebind sessions and purge misrouted caches
- validated token routing and KV cache consistency

Longer term: we will add a safeguard to prevent automated policy failovers from affecting tenant-bound egress (policy gate).

Marissa Cole
VP, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference
